title: Adaptive microbatch trimmer and KV-retention thresholds to stabilize GPU memory under sustained QPS
creator: Avery Chen
description: We are seeing repeated GPU memory churn and transient OOM risk during sustained high QPS bursts on multi-tenant hosts. Current microbatch admission and KV-eviction heuristics are reactive and suffer from oscillation: when KV retention suddenly drops we accept more microbatches so latency spikes, then eviction thrashes. This ticket introduces a lightweight "microbatch trimmer" coupled with an adaptive KV-retention scoring system to proactively shed lower-value microbatches and tighten KV retention thresholds with hysteresis so overall GPU memory usage stabilizes without heavy latency regression for high-priority traffic.
background: Incidents in Feb/Mar show two failure modes: (1) repeated small OOMs during sustained 8k-12k QPS where KV cache growth causes fragmentation and slow compaction, (2) latency tail spikes when the admission controller rapidly oscillates between accepting and rejecting microbatches. Existing work (ENG-24109, ENG-61207) improved admission signaling but did not provide per-microbatch trimming or retention scoring. We need a targeted mitigation that operates inline with the serving runtime and can be toggled per-host/model.
proposed_solution:
Design a microbatch trimmer module in the admission path that:
  - Maintains a short (N=8 sliding window) retention score for each KV namespace (per-model + per-tenant) based on hit-rate, avg seq_len, and last-access recency.
  - Computes an adaptive retention_threshold = baseline * (1 + safety_margin * (1 - retention_score)).
  - When host free GPU memory <= critical_margin, trimmer walks the pending microbatch queue and marks low-priority microbatches for graceful trimming (reduce max_generate_tokens / partial-response) or deferred requeue with exponential backoff.
  - Introduce trimming policies: "gentle-trim" (cut 20-30% of requested tokens), "partial-respond" (return current logits as partial response), and "drop-with-429" (last resort for non-critical requests).
  - Add hysteresis on retention_threshold updates (alpha=0.25, decay window 15s) to avoid oscillation.
  - Expose per-model knobs in the config plane: retention_baseline, safety_margin, allowed_trimming_strategies, and per-request priority weight.

Implementation notes:
  - Integrate with existing admission-controller hooks to avoid a separate scheduling loop.
  - Use lock-free atomic counters for retention scoring; no global locks.
  - Add lightweight telemetry: trimmed_count, trimmed_tokens, average_trim_percent, retention_score_by_namespace.
acceptance_criteria: Under a synthetic sustained QPS 10k test with mixed payloads (0.5/0.3/0.2 short/medium/long), 95th latency decreases by >=10% compared to current baseline while 99.9th latency does not increase by more than 5%
Host-level GPU memory peak reduced by >=15% during the test without increasing overall error rate >0.5%
No new OOM incidents on the canary fleet for 72h under soak testing
Configuration toggles per-model verified via runtime-config and honored within 10s of change
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (dev): add unit tests + microbench harness; implement retention scoring and trimmer behind feature flag
Phase 1 (canary): enable on 5% of serving fleet; run mixed workload soak (48h) with telemetry dashboard
Phase 2 (regional expansion): roll to non-critical regions 25% -> 50% with monitoring alerts in place
Phase 3 (global): enable by default with conservative safety_margin; provide opt-out per-customer for Dedicated/Private
test_plan: Unit tests for retention score calculation and hysteresis behavior
Integration test: admission flow with synthetic KV hit/miss sequences to validate threshold movement
Stress test: replay recorded traffic with injected long sequences to validate trimming reduces peak GPU and avoids OOM
Canary soak: 48h with alert thresholds for CPU/GPU memory and latency; automated rollback if host_oom_events > 0 or error_rate > 0.5%
Chaos test: sudden KV-eviction disabled to simulate cache loss and verify trimmer prevents oscillation
